lessonTitle: Principles of Cancer Treatment: Intent, Cytotoxic Drugs and the Tumour Board

blocks.text: Two patients are both told they have cancer and both are offered chemotherapy. One, a young man with testicular cancer, is being treated to cure him. The other, an 80-year-old woman with widespread metastases, is being treated to keep her comfortable and active for as long as possible. The drugs may look alike; the goal, and therefore the acceptable toxicity, is entirely different.

blocks.markdown: Cancer treatment combines **surgery**, **radiotherapy**, **systemic therapy** (cytotoxic chemotherapy, hormonal, targeted and immunotherapy) and supportive care. Which mix is chosen depends on the tumour type and stage, the patient's fitness and wishes, and above all on the **intent** of treatment.

blocks.title: Curative and palliative intent
blocks.text: **Curative intent** means the aim is to eradicate the cancer and achieve long-term survival without disease, so substantial short-term toxicity is accepted. **Palliative intent** means the aim is to relieve symptoms, maintain quality of life and sometimes prolong survival, without expecting cure, so toxicity must be kept proportionate. **Adjuvant** treatment follows surgery to remove micrometastases; **neoadjuvant** treatment precedes surgery to shrink the tumour.

rows: Symptom control, quality of life, possibly longer survival
Lower; stop if harm exceeds benefit
Localised disease; some metastatic cancers such as testicular germ cell tumours
Incurable metastatic disease; bleeding or pain relief by short radiotherapy
Single-fraction radiotherapy for painful bone metastasis
blocks.caption: Comparing treatment intent.

blocks.markdown: **Cytotoxic chemotherapy** kills cells that are dividing, so it damages rapidly proliferating normal tissues: bone marrow (myelosuppression), gut mucosa (mucositis, diarrhoea), hair follicles (alopecia) and gonads. The nadir of the white cell count usually occurs about 7 to 14 days after a cycle. Drugs are grouped by mechanism. **Alkylating agents**, such as cyclophosphamide, add alkyl groups to DNA, forming cross-links that block replication and cause apoptosis. Cyclophosphamide is activated in the liver; its metabolite acrolein irritates the bladder and causes haemorrhagic cystitis, which is prevented by hydration and mesna.

rows: Block nucleotide synthesis (DHFR or thymidylate synthase)
blocks.caption: Major cytotoxic classes.
Mosteller formula. Many cytotoxic doses are expressed per m^2 of body surface area.

blocks.title: Surface-area dosing (teaching example only)
blocks.prompt: A hypothetical cytotoxic drug is prescribed at 75 mg per m^2. The patient is 160 cm tall and weighs 64 kg. Calculate the body surface area and the dose. This is a teaching example, not a dosing instruction.
blocks.answer: BSA is about 1.69 m^2 and the dose about 126.5 mg.

blocks.caption: ANC is the absolute neutrophil count in 10^9/L; neutropenia is generally an ANC below 1.5, severe below 0.5.

blocks.title: Absolute neutrophil count after chemotherapy
blocks.prompt: Ten days after a cycle a patient has a white cell count of 2.4 x 10^9/L with 25% neutrophils. Calculate the ANC and state the severity.

steps.text: Multiply the white cell count by the neutrophil fraction.
Compare with the thresholds: below 1.5 is neutropenia and below 0.5 is severe.
0.6 is neutropenic but not in the severe range.

blocks.answer: ANC 0.6 x 10^9/L: moderate neutropenia; fever at this stage would need urgent assessment as neutropenic sepsis.

blocks.markdown: **The multidisciplinary team (MDT) or tumour board** is a regular meeting at which specialists review each cancer patient. It exists because treatment choices depend on several kinds of expertise: pathology confirms type and grade, radiology defines stage and resectability, surgeons judge operability, and oncologists advise on drug and radiation options. The MDT agrees a recommended plan with an explicit intent, reduces variation and ensures that comorbidity and performance status are considered. Its recommendations are discussed with the patient, whose informed preferences and consent determine what is actually done.

items: Surgeon, medical oncologist and clinical (radiation) oncologist
Specialist cancer nurse and palliative care input
Coordinator who records decisions and ensures actions follow

blocks.title: Intent first, then toxicity
blocks.text: State the intent of treatment before choosing drugs. Chemotherapy toxicity follows from killing dividing cells, and the MDT recommendation must be reconciled with the patient's wishes.

points: Curative intent accepts greater toxicity to achieve long-term cure; palliative intent prioritises symptoms and quality of life.
Cytotoxic drugs damage rapidly dividing normal tissue; alkylating agents cross-link DNA and cyclophosphamide can cause haemorrhagic cystitis and myelosuppression.
The multidisciplinary tumour board integrates pathology, imaging and clinical judgement into a plan the patient then consents to.

questions.stem: Adjuvant chemotherapy after complete surgical resection of a stage III colon cancer is given with which intent?

options.text: Diagnostic, to determine the tumour type

distractorRationale.b: The tumour has been removed and the aim is cure.

questions.explanation: Adjuvant therapy targets residual microscopic disease after surgery so that cure is more likely. Its intent is curative even though the patient appears disease-free.

questions.stem: A frail 78-year-old with metastatic pancreatic cancer has pain from a rib metastasis. A single fraction of radiotherapy is proposed. Which statement best describes this treatment?

options.text: Palliative: it aims to relieve pain with little treatment burden
Curative: it aims to eradicate all disease

questions.correctOptionText: Palliative: it aims to relieve pain with little treatment burden

distractorRationale.b: Metastatic disease is not curable by one fraction.

questions.explanation: Palliative radiotherapy provides symptom relief with short courses and low toxicity. It does not seek cure in widespread incurable disease.

questions.stem: Why does cyclophosphamide cause haemorrhagic cystitis?

options.text: Its metabolite acrolein irritates the bladder mucosa
It blocks microtubule assembly in the bladder
It inhibits thymidylate synthase in urothelium
It deposits platinum in the kidney

questions.correctOptionText: Its metabolite acrolein irritates the bladder mucosa

distractorRationale.a: Correct; mesna and hydration reduce the risk.

questions.explanation: Cyclophosphamide is metabolised to acrolein, which is excreted in urine and damages the urothelium. Mesna binds acrolein in the bladder and hydration reduces contact time.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old has dyspnoea and an enlarged heart with reduced ejection fraction after several cycles of doxorubicin-containing chemotherapy. Which toxicity is this?
questions.explanation: Anthracyclines cause cardiomyopathy that increases with cumulative dose, so total exposure is tracked and cardiac function monitored. The other toxicities involve different organs.

questions.stem: What is the main function of the multidisciplinary tumour board?

options.text: To integrate pathology, imaging and clinical expertise to recommend a treatment plan
To stage cancer using only blood tests

questions.correctOptionText: To integrate pathology, imaging and clinical expertise to recommend a treatment plan

distractorRationale.d: Staging uses imaging and pathology as well.

questions.explanation: The MDT combines specialist views to define stage, intent and sequence of treatments. Its recommendations are offered to the patient, who decides with their clinician.

questions.stem: A tumour board recommendation is binding on the patient and removes the need for the patient's informed consent.
questions.explanation: The MDT recommends, and the treating clinician discusses options with the patient. Informed consent and patient preference are still required for treatment.

questions.stem: A hypothetical cytotoxic drug (teaching example only) is prescribed at 50 mg/m^2. The patient is 180 cm tall and weighs 80 kg. Using the Mosteller formula, calculate the dose in mg.
questions.explanation: BSA is the square root of (180 x 80 / 3600) = sqrt(4.0) = 2.0 m^2. Dose is 50 mg/m^2 times 2.0 m^2, which is 100 mg.

questions.stem: Ten days after chemotherapy a patient has a white cell count of 1.6 x 10^9/L of which 20% are neutrophils. Calculate the absolute neutrophil count in x 10^9/L. (Severe neutropenia is below 0.5.)
questions.explanation: ANC is 1.6 multiplied by 0.20, which equals 0.32 x 10^9/L. This is below 0.5, so it is severe neutropenia and any fever needs urgent management.

questions.stem: Contrast curative and palliative treatment intent using a 27-year-old with metastatic testicular germ cell tumour and an 84-year-old with metastatic lung cancer and poor performance status. How does intent influence acceptable toxicity?
markingGuide: Define curative intent as aiming for long-term cure
Define palliative intent as symptom relief and quality of life
Testicular germ cell tumour is chemosensitive and potentially curable even when metastatic
Acceptable toxicity is higher for curative intent
Palliative treatment must be proportionate and may be stopped if burdens outweigh benefit
Performance status and patient preference influence choice
Adjuvant or neoadjuvant use is curative intent
questions.explanation: Intent determines the balance of benefit and harm. Marking should reward explicit linking of intent to toxicity tolerance and patient factors.

questions.stem: Explain the mechanism of action of cyclophosphamide and why its main toxicities occur. Include how haemorrhagic cystitis can be prevented.
markingGuide: Prevents DNA replication and triggers apoptosis
Greatest effect on rapidly dividing cells
Myelosuppression with nadir about 7 to 14 days
Mucositis or alopecia from other dividing tissues
questions.explanation: Cytotoxic toxicity reflects loss of dividing normal cells, whereas haemorrhagic cystitis is a metabolite-specific effect. Mesna is the specific protective agent.
